source_time_text: Sep 15, 3:01am FF / linked data released 02:00 UTC

evidence.dominant_driver: China domestic demand remains weak despite a stronger industrial-production print

market_expectations.distribution_notes: The release was expected to show firmer production but still-soft domestic demand.

absorption.reason: About 70 minutes after the 02:00 UTC release, AUS200 was near 8,746, roughly +0.05% on the day and inside a narrow 8,734-8,768 range; the mixed release had not produced a clean directional break.

observations.negative: Retail sales missed, investment deteriorated, unemployment rose, copper was down about 2.2% and AUD was soft.
observations.positive_or_offsetting: Industrial production beat consensus and AUS200 itself remained roughly flat/slightly positive rather than extending lower.

evidence.decision_notes: Forecast is the residual move from the 03:10 UTC decision time, not the original 02:00 UTC data reaction. No M2 learning segment was used to alter confidence because no verified ACTIONABLE model-2 evidence segment specific to this setup was established from the available leakage-safe profile.

immediate.rationale: The China release is internally mixed and AUS200 has shown little net reaction more than an hour after the data.

next_session.rationale: Weak Chinese consumption/investment is offset by stronger production and potential stimulus expectations.

15m.rationale: No clean post-release break; current index action is range-bound.

1h.rationale: Soft retail, deeper investment contraction, higher unemployment and weak copper can weigh on China-sensitive Australian cyclicals if the residual macro signal is repriced.

4h.rationale: Production beat and stimulus expectations can offset the domestic-demand miss, while global oil/rates remain separate headwinds.

next_session.rationale: The mixed China signal lacks enough independent directional force to dominate the next Australian session.

horizons.mechanism: China is Australia's largest trade partner; weaker consumption and investment pressure miners/cyclicals, while stronger factory output partly offsets the demand signal.
horizons.invalidation: A decisive AUS200 breakout above the session range with stronger AUD/copper would invalidate the residual bearish 1h case; a broad China-risk selloff would invalidate the neutral longer-horizon view.
horizons.counter_case: The industrial-production beat may dominate, and weak domestic data may raise expectations for stronger Beijing stimulus, supporting Australian resource and China-sensitive equities.
